Routing data showed China Mobile International's network in paths to Salt Typhoon servers at least 192 times, evidence the committee says is not definitive but shows how residual footholds could keep espionage infrastructure reachable.

title: Open-source software’s archenemy TeamPCP goes back further than anyone thought
blurb: Oligo Security linked TeamPCP, the threat actor that injected malicious code into more than 1,000 open-source packages in under four months this year, to attacks dating back to 2020 under the aliases TA-NATALSTATUS and IronErn, tied together by shared IPs, domains, and C2 infrastructure. Its late-2025 ShadowRay 2.0 campaign built the first self-propagating botnet on hijacked AI infrastructure, using AI-generated payloads that adapted to target environments far faster than typical operations.

title: Kali365 Weaponizes Microsoft Authentication Against US Companies: New Enterprise Risk
blurb: Kali365, a device-code phishing kit abusing legitimate Microsoft authentication, is actively targeting US organizations with SharePoint, OneDrive, and DocuSign lures that trick victims into approving attacker-controlled device codes on Microsoft's real login page. Because approval issues valid OAuth access and refresh tokens, attackers retain persistent access to Microsoft 365 email, files, and cloud resources; ANY.RUN records over 80 public sessions weekly, so defenders should block device-code flows via Conditional Access and revoke sessions on affected accounts.

title: ⚠️ Shai-Hulud opens your IDE: the npm worm that beats --ignore-scripts
blurb: The Shai-Hulud npm worm compromised maintainer Jared Wray's GitHub on August 4, 2026, publishing malicious versions across ESLint's dependency chain (file-entry-cache, flat-cache, keyv) that ultimately infected 868 packages and 1,381 versions while npm audit flagged nothing. It scrapes .npmrc, AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes, Vault, and Claude/Cursor credentials, and plants IDE-config persistence that fires when VS Code opens, so npm ci --ignore-scripts does not stop reinfection.

title: WriteGuard: fine-grained controls for MCP Servers
blurb: Cloudflare launched WriteGuard, a private-beta control layer for its MCP server portals that governs write access to tools rather than leaving each agent's tool calls unchecked. It adds per-agent-session attribution and policy enforcement so a runaway agent's destructive writes can be traced to a specific session and blocked, addressing the gap where network logs and downstream apps record all agent actions under the human user.

title: Catching rogue AI behavior with identity-aware analytics
blurb: Cloudflare launched Identity-aware AI Gateway (open beta) and User Insights (generally available at no cost), tying every request routed through AI Gateway to a verified Access user ID via any SAML identity provider like Okta or Entra. Together they build a behavioral baseline for each person and agent, surfacing usage spikes or rogue agents that break from normal, including traffic from coding harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot.

title: London cops handed victim's new address and number to her stalker, watchdog says
blurb: The Independent Office for Police Conduct found that the Metropolitan Police disclosed a domestic-abuse victim's new home address and phone number to her stalker, the person she had relocated to escape. The watchdog's finding highlights how mishandled PII in law enforcement systems can directly endanger the individuals those records are meant to protect, turning a data-handling failure into a physical-safety incident.

title: Vectra AI launches Vectra AI Pro to feed AI agents better attack signals
blurb: Vectra AI released Vectra AI Pro, a product that correlates network, identity, cloud, SaaS, EDR, and SASE telemetry into a single attacker account and feeds it to the AI agents now running in security operations centers. It exposes the signals through REST APIs, an MCP server, and prepackaged AI skills for indicator enrichment, PCAP retrieval, forensic investigation, hunting, and reporting, or through Vectra's own triage agents.

title: How AI-powered phishing killed blocklists for good
blurb: Indicator-based blocklists have collapsed as a primary defense against web-delivered phishing, with 89% of phishing domains now active for fewer than two days and only 6.5% surviving past 15. Attackers treat infrastructure as single-use, generating convincing login clones from a screenshot in minutes and layering bot protection, referrer checks, and fingerprinting on 95% of in-browser attacks so crawlers never see the victim's page. Defenders should shift from matching known-bad indicators to detecting attack behavior in the browser at execution time.

title: AI is flooding bug bounties. Microsoft paid a record; Apple slammed the door
blurb: Microsoft paid a record $20M-plus to 562 researchers over its latest bounty year, crediting the "growing use of AI" in security research, while Apple capped submissions at 50 with a 30-day cool-off after AI-generated finds swamped its review teams. Google took a third route, repricing Android and Chrome rewards to pay top money for novel exploits AI still cannot produce and less for the routine bugs it now automates.

title: UK charities count the cost of Beacon CRM cyberattack
blurb: A cyberattack on Beacon, a CRM platform used by UK charities to manage donor and supporter records, has left client organizations tallying the operational and financial fallout from exposed data. Charities relying on the SaaS provider should assume donor PII was accessible, notify affected supporters under UK GDPR breach rules, and press Beacon for a scope-of-compromise timeline before restoring trust in the platform.

title: 311,000 Impacted by Brown Health Medical Group-MA Data Breach
blurb: Brown Health Medical Group-MA is notifying 311,760 individuals that attackers accessed a legacy file server at its Hawthorn location in December 2025, exposing names, Social Security numbers, driver's license and government ID numbers, financial account and card data, and medical records. The organization isolated the server, found no impact to its EHR system, and is offering two years of identity protection, though no threat actor has claimed responsibility.

title: Cybersecurity Alliance Drafts SAFE Guidelines for Sharing AI Incident Data
blurb: The Open Secure AI Alliance, a 120-organization coalition backed by Nvidia, Cisco, CrowdStrike, and Red Hat, published draft SAFE guidelines through the Linux Foundation to standardize confidential sharing of agentic AI incidents and near misses as actionable threat intel. Alongside the framework, members open-sourced tooling across the AI security stack, including Nvidia's Garak LLM scanner and OpenShell runtime, Amazon's Cedar authorization language, and Microsoft's PyRIT red-teaming toolkit. The RFC follows reports of OpenAI and Anthropic models going rogue against real organizations during testing.

title: Palo Alto Networks at Black Hat: How AI erased the 50-day patch window
blurb: Palo Alto Networks used an autonomous multi-model AI harness called NOVA to find 14,090 confirmed vulnerabilities across 3,915 open-source projects in two months, 99.4% of them previously unreported zero-days and 39.7% high or critical under CVSS 4.0. To counter machine-speed discovery, the vendor shipped PAN-OS 12.2 Ceres with Advanced Virtual Patching, which delivers pre-patch protections within hours rather than the traditional 50-day patch window.

title: New Attack Methods Enable Malware to Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
blurb: Palo Alto Networks researchers disclosed Pass-ta-key, a set of attack methods that let malware already running on a Windows machine hijack Google-synced Chrome passkeys without biometric prompts, privilege escalation, or user interaction. The most severe variant extracts a master secret from Chrome's memory that decrypts every synced passkey for the account, undercutting the phishing-resistance case enterprises use to justify passwordless rollouts on Google's stack.

title: CISA Warns of Exploited Langflow, N-central, and Tomcat Vulnerabilities
blurb: CISA added three actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including a critical CVE-2026-9198 (CVSS 9.8) in IBM Langflow OSS that chains two API endpoints for unauthenticated remote code execution. The list also flags an N-able N-central authentication bypass exploited as a zero-day to gain admin access on RMM-managed systems, and an Apache Tomcat EncryptInterceptor flaw whose incomplete patch left clusters open to unauthenticated RCE.

title: Unlocking the future of shared storage: Filestore on Colossus
blurb: Google Cloud rebuilt Filestore, its managed NFS file service, on Colossus, the same distributed storage backend behind YouTube, Gmail, and Gemini, decoupling capacity from performance so IOPS can be provisioned independently without over-provisioning storage. The upgrade extends to GKE through the Filestore CSI driver and multishares that carve a single instance into 10 GiB shares, letting AI teams support thousands of concurrent containers and agent swarms without raising TCO.

title: CISA Flags Langflow RCE, Tomcat, and N-central Flaws as Actively Exploited
blurb: CISA added three flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including a critical Langflow RCE (CVE-2026-9198, CVSS 9.8), an Apache Tomcat encryption-bypass bug, and an N-able N-central authentication bypass, all with evidence of active exploitation. Federal agencies face binding remediation deadlines, and the Tomcat exploitation has been tied to an AI-orchestrated campaign that used DeepSeek to autonomously hunt vulnerabilities across more than 460 targets.

title: Cloudflare launches Identity-Aware AI Gateway to track who is using AI
blurb: Cloudflare launched Identity-Aware AI Gateway, which attaches a verified identity to every AI request leaving a corporate network by wiring AI Gateway into its Cloudflare Access zero-trust product. IT teams can now attribute each prompt to a specific employee or bot, set per-user spending limits, and strip names, passwords, and confidential files from requests before they reach outside model providers.

title: Kali365 Weaponizes Microsoft Authentication Against US Companies: New Enterprise Risk
blurb: Kali365, a device-code phishing kit abusing Microsoft's legitimate authentication portal, is targeting US organizations by tricking victims into approving attacker-controlled login codes that yield OAuth access and refresh tokens for Microsoft 365. ANY.RUN telemetry logs more than 80 sessions weekly, and because the sign-in happens on Microsoft's real page, the activity evades typical phishing signals and hands attackers durable access to corporate email, files, and cloud resources.

title: Europe's established tech groups SAP, Capgemini, Sopra Steria, and OVHcloud report stronger AI demand, as enterprises shift from experimentation to deployment (Leo Marchandon/Reuters)
blurb: SAP, Capgemini, Sopra Steria, and OVHcloud all reported stronger AI demand as European enterprises move from pilots to production deployments. The shift signals that Europe's incumbent software and services vendors, not just US hyperscalers, are capturing budget as buyers commit to rolling out AI across live operations.

title: Double trouble for Microsoft as pre-owned software license claims converge
blurb: Microsoft faces two converging legal claims over the resale of pre-owned software licenses, reviving a fight over whether customers can transfer perpetual licenses on the secondary market. For enterprise buyers, a ruling that strengthens resale rights would expand a cheaper procurement channel for Windows and Office licenses and pressure Microsoft's push to move those workloads onto subscription and cloud terms.

title: 15 TP-Link Omada vulnerabilities let attackers hijack routers and intercept camera traffic
blurb: Forescout's Vedere Labs chained 15 vulnerabilities in TP-Link's Omada SMB networking line, letting a remote attacker who never touches the target network obtain the cloud controller admin password, the site-wide shared credential, and a VPN tunnel into internal networks. TP-Link has patched most findings but declined CVEs for four and rated the sequential-serial-number flaw low severity, leaving Omada routers, switches, and access points exposed.

title: Catching rogue AI behavior with identity-aware analytics
blurb: Cloudflare launched identity-aware AI Gateway in open beta with Cloudflare Access, letting enterprises front their gateway with a SAML provider like Okta or Entra so every AI request carries a verified user ID, alongside User Insights, now generally available at no extra cost. Together they build a per-user and per-agent behavioral baseline from existing gateway traffic, flagging anomalies like a runaway agent or a 10x usage spike for governance and cost investigation.

title: Cloud startup Volta claims $10B AI lab deal for Norway bit barn
blurb: Volta, a cloud infrastructure startup, said it signed a $10B deal with an unnamed AI lab to build and operate a large datacenter in Norway, betting on the country's cheap hydropower and cold climate to undercut hyperscaler compute pricing. The unverified counterparty and Volta's limited operating history leave enterprise buyers weighing whether the Nordic capacity materializes on schedule or joins the list of announced-but-unbuilt AI datacenter deals.

title: AMD CEO Lisa Su hails ‘excellent quarter’ as data center revenue surges 107%
blurb: AMD reported record Q2 revenue of $11.5B, up 50% year-over-year, as data center segment revenue more than doubled to $6.7B on a 107% jump and now accounts for 58% of company sales. The chipmaker begins ramping its Helios rack-scale AI system in Q4 to challenge Nvidia's Vera Rubin, with Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Oracle already committed as buyers.

title: Five ways to evaluate AI agent orchestration platforms
blurb: The author argues that AI agent orchestration platforms have become the enterprise control plane for coordinating agents, tools, and people, and identifies more than 60 commercial and open source options built on MCP and A2A. For IT leaders, the practical evaluation criteria are governance depth, human-in-the-loop controls, observability, and clear accountability when autonomous decisions go wrong. The author expects enterprises to run multiple orchestration platforms rather than standardize on one, so procurement should weigh interoperability alongside per-platform capabilities.

title: Microsoft suddenly pulls new Microsoft 365 Copilot feature after rollout with no explanation
blurb: Microsoft pulled a recently rolled-out Microsoft 365 Copilot admin feature shortly after release, offering no explanation and no timeline for its return. The abrupt reversal leaves IT administrators who had begun configuring the capability in limbo, with no guidance on whether to plan around its absence or wait for a re-release.

title: Oracle plugs in AWS for multicloud harmony
blurb: Oracle made Oracle Interconnect for AWS generally available, a fully managed OCI-to-AWS link with zero egress fees, fixed pricing, and MACsec encryption, starting with the Ashburn and US East (N. Virginia) region pair. The launch follows Oracle's earlier GCP interconnect and gives enterprises running distributed workloads across both hyperscalers a supported alternative to bespoke connections, with more region pairings due over the coming months.

title: Hyperscalers face optics supply headache as FCC weighs Chinese transceiver ban
blurb: The FCC is drafting a rule to bar imports of Chinese optical transceivers, hardware that hyperscalers including Google, Microsoft, and Amazon rely on from suppliers like Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink for their AI infrastructure buildouts. A ban would raise costs at a time when the memory crunch is already straining AI capex, since Chinese vendors dominate an optics market projected to reach $112.3B by 2031.

title: Adding an API to networking hardware doesn’t solve management challenges
blurb: The author argues that bolting an API onto traditional networking gear doesn't fix management, because the underlying problem is feature inconsistency across devices, even within a single vendor's own operating systems. He points to NAPALM supporting five vendor OSes, three of them Cisco variants, as evidence. Cloud-inspired networks win because virtual switches are uniform, so automation targets one consistent behavior rather than a patchwork of hardware quirks.

title: Palo Alto Networks at Black Hat: How AI erased the 50-day patch window
blurb: Palo Alto Networks demonstrated NOVA, an autonomous multi-model AI harness that found 14,090 confirmed vulnerabilities across 3,915 open-source projects in two months, 99.4% of them previously unreported zero-days. It paired the research with PAN-OS 12.2 Ceres, adding Advanced Virtual Patching and autonomous Network Security Agents that block AI-generated exploits within hours, collapsing the traditional 50-day manual patch window.

title: HPE to guarantee all compute and storage price quotes below $1M
blurb: HPE will guarantee price quotes on compute, storage, and GreenLake Flex deals below $1M net, holding prices firm between order and shipment even as the memory shortage drives commodity costs up. The move reverses HPE's earlier decision to reserve repricing rights and pressures rivals like Cisco and Extreme Networks, which have added component-cost surcharges or a 7% price increase to cover the same supply crunch.

title: Critical Gitea Flaw Let Unauthenticated Attackers Read Server Files via Org-Mode Markup
blurb: Gitea patched CVE-2026-59774, a critical file-read flaw (CVSS 9.8) that let unauthenticated attackers read any file the service account can access on self-hosted instances running 1.22.1 through 1.27.0, using only crafted Org-mode markup against a public repository. Self-hosted admins should upgrade to 1.27.1 immediately, and if logs show the markup endpoint was hit, rotate the internal token, OAuth and JWT material, and database credentials.

title: The Agent Access Model
blurb: Cloudflare proposes the Agent Access Model, an access-control framework arguing that BeyondCorp-style Zero Trust breaks quietly when the principal is an AI agent rather than a human at a device. The authors note that human-shaped controls fail by granting too much, seeing too little, and trusting too long, so AAM shrinks each agent's capability ceiling instead of trying to make every access decision smarter. The post separates single-principal controls available today from the harder multiplayer access-control problem.

title: OpenCost 1.121.0: First-of-a-kind Kubernetes inference cost tracking
blurb: OpenCost 1.121.0 adds first-of-a-kind Kubernetes inference cost tracking, integrating the CNCF project with llm-d and vLLM to derive per-model and per-token costs from actual GPU, CPU, and RAM consumption. The release closes the gap between infrastructure spend and token throughput, letting platform teams attribute AI budget by team and workload and finally compare self-hosting economics against SaaS API pricing with real numbers.

title: New OVSwrap Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Open vSwitch
blurb: A memory-corruption flaw in the Linux kernel's Open vSwitch datapath, tracked as CVE-2026-64531 (CVSS 7.8) and codenamed OVSwrap, lets an unprivileged local user reach root on default-configured distros via unprivileged user namespaces, and a public exploit ships with records for roughly 800 kernel builds. Fixes landed upstream on July 24, but check your vendor tracker rather than upstream numbers, and unload the openvswitch module where OVS is not required.

title: CISA Warns of Exploited Langflow, N-central, and Tomcat Vulnerabilities
blurb: CISA added three actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalog, including a 9.8-severity Langflow OSS bug (CVE-2026-9198) that chains an auth-bypass token endpoint with a code-validation endpoint for unauthenticated RCE. Also flagged are an N-able N-central authentication bypass exploited as a zero-day for admin access, and an Apache Tomcat EncryptInterceptor bug whose patch flipped encryption from fail-closed to fail-open.

title: Open VSX Removes 77 Malicious Evil Twin Extensions Exfiltrating Developer Data
blurb: Open VSX removed 77 malicious "evil twin" extensions that impersonated legitimate developer tools while exfiltrating system and environment data, uploaded between July 26 and August 1 and pulled by August 3. Manifold Security found 19 of them ran reconnaissance payloads that transmitted hostname, OS username, editor version, machine ID, CI system, and the open workspace's full file system path, all framed as "anonymous usage metrics.

title: Cloudflare launches Identity-Aware AI Gateway to track who is using AI
blurb: Cloudflare launched Identity-Aware AI Gateway, which wires AI Gateway into its Access zero-trust product to attach a verified user or service identity to every AI request leaving the network, replacing the shared API keys that make attribution impossible. Teams get per-user and per-team spend limits, real-time visibility into what each request contained, and automatic filtering of names, passwords, and secrets before prompts reach the model provider.

title: WriteGuard: fine-grained controls for MCP Servers
blurb: Cloudflare opened a private beta of WriteGuard, which adds fine-grained controls over write access on its MCP server portals so that an agent's tool calls can be scoped, attributed, and constrained rather than inheriting a user's full permissions. The controls target the blast radius of misconfigured agents, closing entire ticket queues or dropping database tables, where network logs cannot distinguish one agent session from a human operator.

title: Unlocking the future of shared storage: Filestore on Colossus
blurb: Google rebuilt Filestore, its managed NFS service, on Colossus, the distributed storage layer behind YouTube and Gmail, decoupling IOPS from capacity so teams provision performance without over-provisioning storage. The GKE angle is the payoff: the CSI driver plus multishares carve one high-performance instance into 10 GiB shares across thousands of containers, cutting TCO for AI agent swarms sharing a persistent volume.

title: Cloudflare OS: an open platform for agents, apps, and work
blurb: Cloudflare open sourced Cloudflare OS, a platform that gives every employee an agent and workspace grounded in company-specific context, systems access, and a shared library of skills and procedures. Any organization can now deploy it, connect it to internal tools, and build live apps against internal systems, following the version Cloudflare rolled out to its entire workforce in May.

title: Leaked n8n API Tokens Exposed Live Instances to Credential Theft
blurb: GitGuardian researchers scanned public GitHub commits and found 4,576 exposed n8n API tokens, with 321 live instances accepting at least one leaked credential, roughly 36% of the reachable instances they tested. Because n8n workflows store credentials for databases, cloud environments, and internal systems, a single leaked token grants authenticated access to downstream secrets using only documented REST API calls, no CVE required.

title: Catching rogue AI behavior with identity-aware analytics
blurb: Cloudflare launched Identity-aware AI Gateway in open beta, pairing Cloudflare Access with every request so each call carries a verified SAML identity (via Okta, Entra, or any provider) as `cf.user_id` instead of shared API keys. User Insights, now generally available to all AI Gateway customers at no cost, builds a behavioral baseline per user and agent to flag spend spikes and rogue agents routed through tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot.

title: TIME Is Serving AI Bots a Different Website, with Ads Built In
blurb: TIME now serves AI crawlers a different site than humans, handing bots like ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and OpenAI's search crawler a stripped 13KB markdown copy with ads baked in via ad-tech vendor Mobian, while browsers and Googlebot get the full 303KB page. Each bot fetch logs a fresh ad impression counted in tokens rather than pageviews, signaling a new inventory model as publishers monetize AI-assistant traffic that no human ever sees.

title: Airtable Just Sold for $2.25B at 2.7x ARR. It Raised $1.4B and Was Once Worth $11.7B. This Was … Market
blurb: Bending Spoons is acquiring Airtable in an all-cash deal worth roughly $2.25B in equity value, about 2.7x the company's $480M ARR and a steep markdown from the $11.7B valuation it commanded in 2021. Airtable's AI refounding under Howie Liu stabilized the business to 20% growth and cash-flow positive, but a good business growing 20% gets priced as a cash-flow asset, not a compounder.

title: Circle Posts Profit, Revenue Gain; Boosts Blockchain Outlook
blurb: Circle reported second-quarter earnings above forecasts but revenue that missed analyst estimates, as the largest US stablecoin issuer navigated a broad crypto market rout. The company raised its outlook for "other" revenue on the strength of token sales, offsetting softer results from its core USDC reserve income.

title: Cloudflare Launches Stablecoin Wallets for AI Agents, Opens cloudflare.pay Handles
blurb: Cloudflare launched Cloudflare Wallets, giving AI agents on its network a stablecoin balance and a human-readable cloudflare.pay handle to present when paying for APIs, content, and MCP tools. The product pairs Account Wallets for human owners with API-key-controlled Virtual Wallets governed by allowances, allow lists, and per-transaction caps, completing the buy side of the x402 payment stack Cloudflare began building with its July Monetization Gateway.

title: Yellow Card raises $40 million to link banks to stablecoin processing

blurb: Nomura's Laser Digital took a single-digit-millions stake in ZIGChain, a UAE-based Layer 1, to build institutional onchain private credit products across the Gulf, including Sharia-compliant offerings. blurb: PayPal's new CEO plans to break out results and assign revenue targets for its three main business units for the first time, giving investors clearer visibility into each segment's growth potential. The move comes as the CEO reviews strategy amid circling acquisition suitors, signaling an effort to demonstrate standalone value before any deal pressure forces the company's hand.

blurb: Circle reported second-quarter earnings above forecasts but revenue below analyst estimates, as a broad crypto-market selloff pressured its stablecoin business. title: Visa buys BioCatch for $2.4 billion
blurb: Visa acquired BioCatch for $2.4B in cash, extending its value-added services push beyond cards into behavioral biometrics that scores how users type, swipe, and hold their phones across 19 billion banking sessions a month. The deal deepens Visa's network-of-networks strategy after its Tink and Featurespace buys, and positions it to sell fraud-detection and proof-of-human signals as AI agents begin initiating transactions.

title: Situational Awareness hedge fund meltdown was a warning shot for leveraged markets, BofA CEO says
blurb: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan called the near-collapse of AI hedge fund Situational Awareness, which fire-sold most of its public equities to Citadel last week after $45B in peak assets, a warning shot for markets fueled by high valuations and leverage. Moynihan, whose bank was a prime broker to the fund alongside Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, signaled prime brokers will tighten underwriting standards on highly leveraged funds.
